units.distance: hundredths of a foot, from the gate along the rail
units.lane: hundredths of a lane, 0 is the rail

lapFeet.note: One-mile dirt oval. Marked confirmed because the lead checked it on 2026-11-11 against the track's own site, the track's own site, which describes a one-mile dirt oval. Joseph has not confirmed it yet.

runUpFeet.note: No run-up modeled yet. Distance is measured from the gate.

stretchFeet.note: From memory, not confirmed by a primary source. Measured from the end of the last turn to the wire.

turnFeet.note: Each of the two turns: what is left of the mile after both straights, split evenly. A 10 furlong race (6600 ft) starts 1320 ft before the wire, so the field passes the wire once and then runs one full lap. That puts the gate in the last turn, just behind the head of the stretch. All of this layout is a guess.

askFeetToGo.note: Stalkers and closers ask at about the 5/16 pole, so an M1.4 move at the 3/8 pole is a real change. Front-runners kick on a little earlier, which kept the three styles within the fairness tolerance.

cruiseFeetPerSecond.note: Set so the shipped card's median winning time at 10 furlongs on fast dirt is about 2:01.5.

formSpeedShare.note: Kept small: when form moved speed a lot, a hot half mostly meant a front-runner having a good day.

frontRunnerPace.note: Short presses and a costly duel, so a hot half usually means front-runners fought and paid for it.

kickBoostShare.note: Steep on purpose so +10 kick is worth about as much as +10 speed or stamina; a kick-70 horse still gets 6.5 percent. Below kick 41 the line goes negative and the sim treats it as no extra gear.

laneWidthFeet.note: Narrower than a horse on purpose: at 2 feet, 8 identical horses showed the inside posts winning about 2.5 points too often.
